extracted.intended_audience: federal agency standards executives, rule writers, policy staff implementing OMB Circular A-119 and the NTTAA
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and required reporting format for federal agencies implementing OMB Circular A-119 / NTTAA: how agencies must consider, use, substitute, report on, and provide for participation in voluntary consensus standards in rulemaking, procurement, and agency practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: OSHA Act Section 6 rule-difference publication requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: "Whenever a rule promulgated by the Secretary differs substantially from an existing national consensus standard, the Secretary shall, at the same time, publish in the Federal Register a statement of the reasons why the rule as adopted will better effectuate the purposes of this Act than the national consensus standards."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory requirement explains OSHA's active involvement in consensus standards committees; agencies must provide a contemporaneous Federal Register statement explaining why departing from a consensus standard is preferable.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPSC deferral to voluntary standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Consumer Product Safety Act (as amended), the Commission must defer to issued voluntary standards, rather than promulgate mandatory standards, when the voluntary standards would eliminate or adequately reduce the risk of injury addressed and it is likely that there will be substantial compliance with the voluntary standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to deferral, the Commission must provide technical and administrative assistance after notice (or ANPRM) to persons or groups proposing to develop or modify an appropriate voluntary standard, and is encouraged to provide assistance taking into account Commission resources and priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Circular A-119 reporting element 1: participation counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the number of voluntary consensus standards bodies in which the agency participates, and the number of agency employees participating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies report participation by operating administration/component (examples in the report show counts of employees and groups per agency). Also note roles such as serving as officers on boards and committees.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Circular A-119 reporting element 2: voluntary standards used
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the number of voluntary consensus standards the agency has used since the relevant reporting date (e.g., since October 1, 1997) based on the procedures set forth in sections 11 and 12 of the Circular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include standards incorporated by reference in regulations and other uses (e.g., EPA reported number of final regulations incorporating voluntary standards and numbers of standards cited in proposed rules). Distinguish regulatory use from procurement use if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Circular A-119 reporting element 3: substitutions identified
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify voluntary consensus standards that have been substituted for government-unique standards as a result of an agency review under section 15b(7) of the Circular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific examples when substitutions occurred (the report lists FAA, NHTSA, DOT examples such as AMS/NAS/SAE items and SAE Recommended Practices). Describe scope and regulatory docket references where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Circular A-119 reporting element 4: evaluation and recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an evaluation of the effectiveness of Circular A-119 policy and any recommendations for changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should assess whether Circular A-119 is working effectively, the benefits (e.g., saving time and money), and offer recommended changes or note lack thereof (several agencies in the report state the Circular is effective or needs no changes).

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Circular A-119 reporting element 5: instances of government-unique use
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify all instances when the agency used government-unique standards in lieu of voluntary consensus standards; for each instance include agency rationale and the specific government-unique standard used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the rationale and citations (the report gives NHTSA NPRM example regarding ANSI Z535.4 and agency choices for label colors based on focus group results).

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA rulemaking practice for considering voluntary consensus standards
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA regulators should routinely consider the use of voluntary consensus standards in proposed and final Agency regulations, summarize NTTAA requirements in preambles, explain how they searched for potentially applicable voluntary consensus standards, and describe tentative or final decisions about their use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA developed an "EPA Rule Writer’s Guide to the NTTAA" explaining procedures to systematically assess standards for proposed and final rules; EPA also promotes use of model language to aid electronic tracking of consideration/use of standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA ethics and employee participation guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA revised Agency ethics guidance to reconcile criminal conflict-of-interest provisions with the NTTAA directive that Federal employees participate in standards-setting activities, providing a pathway for EPA employee membership in standards development organizations including serving on boards and as committee chairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidance (issued Sept 1998) relies on OLC and OGE memoranda and clarifies when and how employees may participate; agencies should maintain and distribute such guidance and attach it to standards programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case-by-case principle for conflicts between voluntary standards and other evidence (NHTSA labeling example)
rubrics_metrics.description: When voluntary consensus standards (e.g., ANSI) conflict with other evidence such as focus group results, agencies should recognize differing missions (e.g., comprehensive hazard hierarchy vs. designing an effective label for a specific hazard) and make case-by-case determinations guided by facts of the specific hazard, agency expertise, and judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NHTSA solicited comments on whether colors and signal words should be guided by focus group preferences versus the ANSI standard and noted it would rely on expertise and statutory provisions to make determinations; agencies should document such analyses in rulemaking records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards program coordination and oversight duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should appoint a Standards Executive/Voluntary Standards Coordinator to establish agency views on standards issues, provide oversight for staff involvement in voluntary standards activities, coordinate participation, and meet reporting requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: CPSC's Voluntary Standards Coordinator provides reports and oversight; EPA's Standards Executive represents the Agency on interagency committees and works with General Counsel and program offices to implement NTTAA/Circular A-119.
